brief: Second version of the Stormwood hero Stormheart Tree, replacing cand3's silo/water-tower read
flag: flag-off: CANDIDATE until its scene passes three-judge Bar A review
author: Claude (coordinator-side Meshy prop worker), owner-authorized Meshy use (Standing owner direction 1, 15 Oct 2026); existing license, no purchase
judges_asks: Three code-blind judges read cand3 as a 'silo / water tower' with a 'cotton-candy blue crown'.
Visibly SPLIT, gnarled trunk: ancient storm-split giant, trunk divided into two or three great limbs with a lightning-scarred cleft.
GREENER, DENSER crown: deep storm-forest greens with a few faint cyan storm-glow accents, not a blue puff.
Must read as an enormous ancient tree at distance.
how_addressed: Concept prompts forbid blue/teal foliage and require a low V/trident split with a charred, cyan-lit cleft; chosen model shows the V cleft from front and back and a deep-green clumped crown (cyan only as faint accents). Side profile is still narrower than the front (crown depth ~72% of width).
replaces: stormheart_tree cand3 (task 01a15c4c-147d-77f1-99b0-5d0855a8589a) - judged silo-like; this asset is an alternative, cand1-3 untouched
workflow: agent-drafted multi-view concept from repo reference boards (Meshy image-to-image nano-banana-pro, refs as data URIs) -> inspected by worker -> Meshy image-to-3d (latest, quad remesh, 150k target, PBR textures embedded in GLB)

native_size.note: Meshy raw GLB, ~1.9 units tall, Y up, centre origin

scale_normalisation.method: lossless: GLB scene roots wrapped in node 'metres_root' with uniform scale + translation; BASE AT y=0, footprint centred on x/z (no centre-origin sink)
scale_normalisation.note: Uniform scale gives 196.8 x 141.2 m crown footprint at 260 m tall; reaching 250 m spread needs extra horizontal scale (~1.27x X / ~1.77x Z) or accepting the narrower crown. Gameplay hollow/passages/rings are not modelled; lane geometry stays authoritative.

materials: single material Material_0, embedded baseColor + metallicRoughness + normal textures (3 images); separate PBR maps not kept (disk)
palette_check: deep greens, dark brown-grey bark, aged copper trim, cyan-white scar glow, one navy banner; no red/oxblood

previews: preview_3view.png (software flat-shaded front / 40 deg / side, colours sampled per face)
files.raw_glb: not published (identical mesh minus metres_root node)

concept_tasks.verdict: View 0 REJECTED (narrow lollipop / tower silhouette). Views 1-2: broad dense deep-green crown on three limbs, split readable but subtle. View 1 modelled as m_c2v1.
Strong V split with lightning-scarred cleft and green crown, but crown sparse; views inconsistent (view 2 a different tree). View 0 modelled as alternate m_c1v0.

reference_paths: local: concepts/c1_0.png (own concept c1, view 0: deep V lightning split)
local: concepts/c2_1.png (own concept c2, view 1: broad dense green crown)
concept_tasks.verdict: CHOSEN source: merge of c1 split + c2 crown (refs c1_0, c2_1, b_exterior). View 1 best: deep V lightning cleft with cyan-white glow, one broad dense deep-green canopy with a few faint cyan accents, gnarled bark, buttress roots. View 0 side view narrower (lollipop-leaning) so not used alone.

model_tasks.verdict: alternate, not published: most open V split (limbs diverge), but crown thinner and side-flat (depth/width 0.70).
rejected: dense green crown but split hard to read; slab-like side (depth/width 0.64).
CHOSEN: clear V lightning cleft with glowing scar visible front and back, dense deep-green crown, no blue puff, no red; depth/width 0.72.
rejected: see-through split reads well from front, but flattest (depth/width 0.55) and thin tower-like side view.

verdict_worker: Preview-level only, not yet judged in engine. Reads as a giant storm-split oak: V cleft with glowing scar and rope bridge, gnarled twisted bark, buttress roots, dense deep-green canopy. Weaknesses: side profile narrower than front; cleft glow is texture-only (pair with the lane's energy-seam VFX).
